newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 12.97 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 12.97 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 55 basis points to 12.97 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 40 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 13.52 percent coupon for a price of 100.26 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 13.52 percent.

The bank also sold ten billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 13.74 percent coupon at a price of 99.12 percent, and ten billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 13.97 percent coupon at an average price of 98.27 percent.
Yields for these notes fell one basis points to 15.05 percent for the 269-day bills, and four basis points to 15.99 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
